title: Comparative Study of Virtual-Reality–Supported and Recorded Hygiene Training to Improve Home Kitchen Hygiene
summary:
Background
Many foodborne illnesses originate in private households. This often happens because foods may carry natural or harmful microorganisms, and essential hygiene rules are not always followed in the kitchen. These rules include, for example, thorough handwashing or avoiding contamination between raw and ready-to-eat foods. To help people better understand and apply such rules, different types of hygiene training exist. One modern approach is learning in a virtual environment (“virtual reality”), where situations can be presented very realistically. However, it is still largely unknown whether such VR-based training leads to better understanding and behaviour compared to a recorded video lecture.

Research Question
The study aims to determine whether training in a virtual kitchen leads to better hygiene knowledge and more hygienic behaviour than traditional video-based training. It will also examine whether individual differences, such as age or personality, affect how well the training works. In addition, the study investigates how the trainings influence psychological well-being.

Methods
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:
• One group receives training in a virtual kitchen where they prepare a simple dish.
• The other group watches a recorded presentation on hygiene topics.

Before the training, immediately afterwards, and again two weeks later, participants complete questionnaires on hygiene knowledge and well-being. In addition, samples are collected from various surfaces in participants’ own kitchens and from the palm of their hand. These samples indicate how many and which microorganisms are present and whether changes occur after the training.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- At least 18 years old
- Own kitchen available
- Sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaires
- Written consent to participate in the study and for data collection
Exclusion criteria:
- Psychological and mental illnesses, such as anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, or severe depression
- Medical contraindications, such as severe vision impairment, migraines, or epilepsy
- Cognitive impairments, such as dementia
- Addictive disorders, such as VR or computer game addiction
